reasoning: Both attempts split the panel into a side-effect-free view and keep the effects out of the story. Only B moves the WaitForChild yield out of the component body: it runs the wait in a spawned thread with cleanups on both the thread and the connection. A leaves the yield unchanged inside buildModeHud, which fails a core part of the task.

criteria.criterion: Valid UI Labs Vide story with live controls
criteria.note: `UILabs.CreateVideStory({vide = Vide, controls = ...})` with a Choose built from `BlockTypes.List`, a String control for the name and a Number control for the count, each passed to the view as a live source; there is no shortcut for trying a long name.
BuildModeHudView takes `playerName`, `selectedBlock` and `placedCount` as sources, and BuildModeHud supplies LocalPlayer, the BlockPlacer selection and the remote count.

criteria.criterion: No yield inside a Vide scope
criteria.note: The unchanged `ReplicatedStorage:WaitForChild("BlockPlaced")` still runs synchronously in the `buildModeHud` component body; the story avoids it, but the yield was never moved out of the scope.

criteria.criterion: Effects kept out of the story and undone in game
criteria.note: The blur, zoom and sound stay in BuildModeHud with their existing cleanups, and the story renders only BuildModeHudView.
The wrapper keeps every effect and feeds the same live sources, so the HUD looks and updates as before.
All checks pass, the story never yields or touches game state, and the Props type is clear.

criteria.criterion: Valid UI Labs Vide story with live controls
criteria.note: Returns `{vide = Vide, controls = CONTROLS, story = story}` with `Ordered` Choose, String and Slider controls, all live; long names are only mentioned in a comment.
Props accept either a value or a source (read through `read`), and the story and the wrapper each supply them.

criteria.criterion: No yield inside a Vide scope
criteria.note: The WaitForChild call moves into `task.spawn`, with cleanups registered on both the thread and the connection, so the component body no longer yields.

criteria.criterion: Effects kept out of the story and undone in game
criteria.note: The blur, zoom and sound stay only in the game wrapper with their cleanups intact.
The name, the selection (through `BlockTypes.ByName`) and the count still update, and the effects still run.
Uses strict mode with a typed StoryProps, and all checks pass; the `@game/` string requires and `const` syntax are less conventional.

strengths: Clean split into a pure view and a game-side wrapper
Simple, readable story built with CreateVideStory
weaknesses: The WaitForChild yield is left inside the component body
